newsitem.title: BRAZIL: ATHLETICS-KENYA'S TERGAT WINS SILVESTRE AGAIN.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-KENYA'S TERGAT WINS SILVESTRE AGAIN.

text.p: Kenya's Paul Tergat, silver medallist in the 10,000 metres at this year's Atlanta Olympics, strode away on his own to win the Sao Silvestre 15 kilometre road race for the second year running on Tuesday.
Tergat, the reigning world cross country champion, broke the resistance of compatriot Joseph Kimani, his only serious challenger, around 1,500 metres from the end of the traditional end-of-year race.

He broke away to win in 43 minutes 50 seconds, finishing more than half a minute ahead of Kimani who completed the race in 44.23. Brazil's Vanderley Cordeiro de Lima was third, a further 33 seconds back.
The two Kenyans had the race to themselves from the ten-kilometre mark, by which time they had opened an 18-second lead over Cordeiro and the rest of the pack.
They then ran side by side until Kimani cracked going up the punishing 1,800 metre long Brigadeiro hill.
It was the third time in the last four years Kenya have won the race, which has been run through the streets of Latin America's largest city on New Year's Eve every year since 1925.

Tergat, who set a new race record of 43.12 seconds when he won last year, announced last week that 1997 will probably his last year as a serious track athlete and that he plans to take up the marathon from 1998.
